title: Enable paccache.timer to prune the pacman cache weekly
head: 98898d3ad367
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: Three findings: timer duplicates update-time keep-2 prune (normally a no-op, wording wrong); migration filename collides with open #11558 (add/add conflict either order); failed enable marked complete (minor, collapsed). Related open #6553 noted.

leads.summary: Open PR #11558 adds a different migration under the identical 1789156273.sh filename
leads.consequence: These non-stacked PRs have an add/add conflict. A naive manual resolution keeping either file drops the other's repair. A resolution that puts both bodies under this one filename but ships after a user has already recorded ~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/1789156273.sh still cannot deliver the later-added repair. Allocate a unique migration identifier for one PR before either ships.
leads.triage: new lead, factual; verified by coordinator (gh api file lists; verify/pr11558*.json) and merge reproducer (verify/merge-repro, add/add conflict both orders); Opus self-check independently ran merge-tree with same result; published

leads.summary: Failed enable is logged but recorded as a completed migration
leads.consequence: On a missing/masked unit, failed sudo authentication, or other systemctl enable failure, the warning branch succeeds. The runner writes the per-user marker and goes on with subsequent migrations and update steps; --pending then returns no work and a later update skips this migration, leaving cache maintenance disabled unless another user's separate marker causes a retry or the user manually clears the marker. Forward a nonzero exit after a useful error to keep it retryable, or explicitly verify successful enablement before exiting.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Finding 2); corroboration; published collapsed

leads.summary: The is-enabled guard treats a temporary runtime enable as durable
leads.consequence: On a machine where someone previously ran `systemctl enable --runtime paccache.timer`, systemctl is-enabled --quiet returns success for enabled-runtime; this migration neither enables the timer persistently nor checks again and the runner records completion. Runtime enable symlinks disappear on reboot, so no weekly cleanup is scheduled thereafter. Distinguish the printed enabled state from enabled-runtime, rather than treating any zero status as permanent enablement. The same upstream predicate accepts static/alias/indirect/generated states, so a customized replacement could also bypass this guard.
leads.triage: dropped: implausible administrator state, no demonstrated impact

leads.summary: The system-service acceptance fixture omits the newly required timer
leads.consequence: `verify_services` enumerates required enabled system units but not paccache.timer. An installed machine with a missing/disabled timer would pass this service audit even though scheduled cleanup is absent. Add paccache.timer to the list of units checked with systemctl is-enabled; there is no need to assert that its one-shot service is continuously active.
leads.triage: checked, not a gap: list is a subset (cups, linux-modules-cleanup, systemd-oomd also absent); dropped

leads.summary: The new shell assertion never exercises the upgrade migration
leads.consequence: A plausible regression that drops migrations/1789156273.sh (or changes its guarded enable into a no-op) still passes the only new test because it greps solely the fresh-install script. Add a focused migration test using stubbed systemctl/sudo and the actual migrator, asserting successful enablement, idempotence, and that failed enable leaves a pending marker. Existing migrations have such tests in test/shell.d/.
leads.triage: dropped as generic test request; migration failure covered by Finding 2 reproducer

leads.summary: The migration's rationale incorrectly says existing installs have retained every downloaded version
leads.consequence: Normal existing installs already run `omarchy-update-pkg-prune`, which calls sudo paccache -rk2 before every update snapshot. The new timer can help between updates or on paths that bypass Omarchy's update, but it is not the first bound on existing installations' pacman cache. Correct the rationale and account for the existing two-version retention and snapshot ordering when explaining the weekly three-version timer. This is a contradicted premise, not proof the timer is unnecessary.

leads.summary: Open PR #6553 also enables paccache.timer and conflicts in the installer hunk
leads.consequence: PR #6553 adds the same systemctl enable paccache.timer in this exact region and its own migration to enable it on existing systems, in addition to journal and Btrfs changes. Both PRs are non-stacked, and a merged installer file has a conflict at the overlapping hunk, so reconcile the two definitions into a single enable line and avoid redundant cache migration work if #6553 is revived. #6553 is currently CONFLICTING against its base even without this PR; do not mistake it for an already-merged dependency.
leads.triage: already in Opus final; corroboration; published collapsed

## Automated AI review > **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review. **Outcome:** `omarchy update` already prunes the pacman cache, so this timer normally removes nothing. ### Timer duplicates the update-time prune `bin/omarchy-update` runs `paccache -rk2` (from #6734) before every package update, leaving at most 3 versions per package after a normal update, so the keep-3 timer finds nothing. It prunes mainly if `omarchy update` is bypassed. **Impact:** low, but it adds a second cache policy, and the migration's messages say the cache grows unbounded. **Suggested change:** State what the timer adds beyond that prune and fix the wording, or rely on the existing prune.
Reproducer (paccache 1.13.1 on a temporary directory) ```bash #!/bin/bash # What paccache.timer finds on a cache that `omarchy update` already pruned. # paccache.service runs `paccache -r $PACCACHE_ARGS`; PACCACHE_ARGS is empty in # the shipped /etc/conf.d/pacman-contrib, so it keeps 3 versions per package. # omarchy-update-pkg-prune runs `paccache -rk2` before every package update. # Needs pacman-contrib. Touches only a temporary directory. set -euo pipefail cache=$(mktemp -d) trap 'rm -rf "$cache"' EXIT add() { for v in "$@"; do printf x >"$cache/foo-$v-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst"; done; } show() { ls -1 "$cache" | sed 's/^/ /'; } add 1.0-1 1.1-1 1.2-1 1.3-1 1.4-1 echo "Cache before the first omarchy update:" show for next in 5 6 7; do echo echo "## omarchy update: omarchy-update-pkg-prune (paccache -rk2)" paccache -rk2 -c "$cache" --nocolor add "1.$next-1" echo "## the update downloads foo-1.$next-1" echo "## paccache.timer fires: paccache -r (keep 3)" paccache -r -c "$cache" --nocolor show done echo echo "## Control: the same timer run on a cache nothing else pruned" rm -f "$cache"/* add 1.0-1 1.1-1 1.2-1 1.3-1 1.4-1 paccache -r -c "$cache" --nocolor show ``` Actual output (exit 0): ```text Cache before the first omarchy update: foo-1.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.1-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.2-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.3-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.4-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst ## omarchy update: omarchy-update-pkg-prune (paccache -rk2) ==> finished: 3 packages removed (disk space saved: 3 B) ## the update downloads foo-1.5-1 ## paccache.timer fires: paccache -r (keep 3) ==> no candidate packages found for pruning foo-1.3-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.4-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.5-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst ## omarchy update: omarchy-update-pkg-prune (paccache -rk2) ==> finished: 1 packages removed (disk space saved: 1 B) ## the update downloads foo-1.6-1 ## paccache.timer fires: paccache -r (keep 3) ==> no candidate packages found for pruning foo-1.4-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.5-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.6-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst ## omarchy update: omarchy-update-pkg-prune (paccache -rk2) ==> finished: 1 packages removed (disk space saved: 1 B) ## the update downloads foo-1.7-1 ## paccache.timer fires: paccache -r (keep 3) ==> no candidate packages found for pruning foo-1.5-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.6-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.7-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst ## Control: the same timer run on a cache nothing else pruned ==> finished: 2 packages removed (disk space saved: 2 B) foo-1.2-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.3-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst foo-1.4-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst ```
### Migration name collides with #11558 Open #11558 adds a different `migrations/1789156273.sh`, and its test uses that name. **Impact:** whichever lands second hits an add/add conflict, in either order. **Suggested change:** Use a fresh migration timestamp.
Reproducer (merges onto the quattro base branch at 8b4eae6; #11558 at b0477ee) ```bash #!/bin/bash # Merge #11523 and #11558 onto quattro in both orders, in a throwaway clone. set -uo pipefail work=$(mktemp -d) trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT git clone -q --bare --filter=blob:none https://github.com/omacom/omarchy.git "$work/repo" cd "$work/repo" git fetch -q origin quattro pull/11523/head:pr11523 pull/11558/head:pr11558 for order in "pr11523 pr11558" "pr11558 pr11523"; do set -- $order echo "## quattro + $1, then $2" first=$(git merge-tree --write-tree quattro "$1") || { echo "first merge failed"; continue; } first_commit=$(git commit-tree "$first" -p quattro -p "$1" -m first) git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only "$first_commit" "$2" | tail -n +2 echo "exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}" done ``` Actual output (exit 0): ```text ## quattro + pr11523, then pr11558 migrations/1789156273.sh Auto-merging migrations/1789156273.sh CONFLICT (add/add): Merge conflict in migrations/1789156273.sh exit: 1 ## quattro + pr11558, then pr11523 migrations/1789156273.sh Auto-merging migrations/1789156273.sh CONFLICT (add/add): Merge conflict in migrations/1789156273.sh exit: 1 ```
More findings ### A failed enable is recorded as complete `as_root systemctl enable --now ... || echo "Could not enable ..."` exits 0, so `omarchy-migrate` writes the marker and never retries. `agents/skills/migrations.md` says a migration that cannot finish must exit non-zero and stay pending. **Impact:** low; the earlier systemd-oomd migration uses the same pattern. **Suggested change:** Exit 0 quietly when the unit is masked or not installed, exit non-zero on other enable failures, and keep the error text visible. Reproducer (save as `test/shell.d/paccache-timer-migration-test.sh`; fails at `98898d3`): ```bash #!/bin/bash set -euo pipefail source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh" test_tmp=$(mktemp -d) trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT migration=1789156273.sh stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin" omarchy_root="$test_tmp/omarchy" test_home="$test_tmp/home" mkdir -p "$stub_bin" "$omarchy_root/migrations" "$test_home" cp "$ROOT/migrations/$migration" "$omarchy_root/migrations/" # The timer is not enabled yet, and sudo cannot authenticate (wrong password, # no terminal, cancelled prompt). cat >"$stub_bin/systemctl" <<'STUB' #!/bin/bash printf 'systemctl %s\n' "$*" >>"$CALLS" [[ $1 == "is-enabled" ]] && exit 1 exit 0 STUB cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'STUB' #!/bin/bash printf 'sudo %s\n' "$*" >>"$CALLS" echo "sudo: a password is required" >&2 exit 1 STUB cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-notification-dismiss" <<'STUB' #!/bin/bash exit 0 STUB chmod +x "$stub_bin"/* run_migrate() { CALLS="$test_tmp/calls" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" HOME="$test_home" OMARCHY_PATH="$omarchy_root" \ "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-migrate" "$@" } run_migrate >"$test_tmp/out" 2>&1 || true sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' -e '/^$/d' -e 's/^/ | /' "$test_tmp/out" grep -Fx 'sudo systemctl enable --now paccache.timer' "$test_tmp/calls" >/dev/null || fail "migration asks sudo to enable paccache.timer" pass "migration asks sudo to enable paccache.timer" run_migrate --pending >/dev/null || fail "paccache.timer migration stays pending when it could not enable the timer" pass "paccache.timer migration stays pending when it could not enable the timer" ``` Actual output (exit 1): ```text | Running migration (1789156273) | Prune the pacman package cache weekly to prevent unbounded disk growth | Could not enable paccache.timer; package cache will continue to grow unbounded. ok - migration asks sudo to enable paccache.timer not ok - paccache.timer migration stays pending when it could not enable the timer ``` ### Related open PR #6553 also adds `systemctl enable paccache.timer` at the same place in `install/config/enable-services.sh` plus its own enable migration.
Verified - `paccache.timer` and `paccache.service` ship in `pacman-contrib`, which is in `install/omarchy-base.packages`. - The installer line enables without `--now`, like the other lines in `enable-services.sh`. - The migration skips sudo when the timer is already enabled (second user on the machine). - The new `systemd-test.sh` assertion passes at head and fails with the line removed. - `systemd-test.sh`, `update-pkg-prune-test.sh`, `migrate-scope-test.sh` and `./test/cli` pass at head.
